lessons.title: What crypto is
lessons.description: A ledger, a key, and a wallet: the whole idea in three minutes.

exercises.prompt: What is a blockchain, in plain terms?

options.text: A shared ledger that many computers keep in sync
A bank account that pays interest

exercises.explanation: A blockchain is a ledger copied across many machines, so no single party can rewrite it quietly.

exercises.prompt: True or false?
exercises.statement: Crypto assets are only useful for speculation.
exercises.explanation: They also carry payments, access, and identity use cases. Speculation is one use, not the only one.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence about ownership.
parts: A crypto asset sits in a
, and control of it comes from a
exercises.explanation: The wallet holds the address; the key proves you may move what is there.

exercises.prompt: Match each key with how it should be treated.
exercises.explanation: The public address receives funds. The private key moves them, so it stays secret.

lessons.title: Wallets and keys
lessons.description: Backups, seed phrases, and the mistakes that cannot be undone.

exercises.prompt: You lose your private key and have no backup. What happens?

options.text: You lose access to that wallet

exercises.explanation: Self-custody means nobody can reset your key for you. The backup is the recovery plan.

exercises.prompt: Put safe wallet setup in order.

steps.text: Open a wallet app you trust
Write the seed phrase on paper, offline

exercises.explanation: Create, back up offline, then test with a small amount before trusting it with more.

exercises.prompt: Complete the backup rule.
exercises.explanation: Paper or metal, offline. Photos and cloud notes are easy to steal.

exercises.prompt: What do you do next?
exercises.body: A 'wallet inspector' DMs you: 'Your wallet is at risk. Send your seed phrase so I can secure it.'
exercises.explanation: No legitimate service needs your seed phrase. Anyone who asks is attacking you.

lessons.title: Reading a candle
lessons.description: Open, high, low, close: what one candle tells you.

exercises.prompt: Which candle closed weakest relative to its open?
exercises.explanation: Candle 2 opened at 105 and closed at 92, giving up the most ground.

exercises.prompt: What do the thin wicks above and below a candle show?

options.text: The highest and lowest prices in that period

exercises.explanation: Wicks mark the extremes reached before the period closed.

exercises.prompt: True or false?
exercises.statement: A green candle guarantees the price will keep rising.
exercises.explanation: One candle describes the past. It never guarantees the next move.

exercises.prompt: Put a simple candle read in order.

steps.text: Note where it opened and closed
Note the high and low wicks
Compare it with the previous candle

exercises.explanation: Body, wicks, then context. A candle alone is not a signal.

lessons.title: Support and resistance
lessons.description: The price levels where buyers and sellers keep showing up.

exercises.prompt: What is support?

options.text: A price area where buyers have repeatedly stepped in
A guarantee that price cannot fall further
The highest price of the year

exercises.explanation: Support is a zone of past demand, not a floor that cannot break.

exercises.prompt: Match each level with its usual nickname.
exercises.explanation: Support sits below price, resistance above. Either can break.

exercises.prompt: Price bounced near which level three times?
exercises.explanation: Each low lands near 100, which is the support zone being tested.

exercises.prompt: What is the calmer choice?
exercises.body: Price just closed below a support level you have watched for weeks. A friend says it is 'free money' to buy now.
exercises.explanation: Broken support often becomes resistance. Waiting for confirmation costs less than guessing.

lessons.title: Dollar-cost averaging
lessons.description: Buying on a schedule instead of guessing the perfect moment.

exercises.prompt: You follow a fixed weekly plan. What is the right action at each price shown?
exercises.explanation: A fixed plan buys the same amount on schedule. Price swings do not change the rule.

exercises.prompt: What does dollar-cost averaging mean?

options.text: Buying a fixed amount on a fixed schedule
Buying only after a big drop

exercises.explanation: DCA spreads purchases over time, so one entry price does not decide your outcome.

exercises.prompt: You risk 1% of a 1000 unit balance with entry at 100 and stop at 95. What position size should you take?
exercises.explanation: Risk is 10. Each unit risks 5, so buy 2 units: a 200 position.

exercises.prompt: True or false?
exercises.statement: Dollar-cost averaging removes the risk of losing money.
exercises.explanation: It reduces timing risk only. The asset can still fall.

lessons.title: Time in the market
lessons.description: Why patience and compounding beat reaction.

exercises.prompt: Why does time in the market usually beat timing the market?

options.text: Missing the best days hurts long-run returns

exercises.explanation: A few strong days carry a lot of the long-run return, and they are impossible to predict.

exercises.prompt: Complete the compounding sentence.
exercises.explanation: Returns earning returns needs time, and time needs patience.

exercises.prompt: What do you do?
exercises.body: Your portfolio drops 20% in a week. A headline says the market is finished.

options.text: Re-read your plan and stick to it

exercises.explanation: A written plan made before the drop is calmer than a headline made during it.

exercises.prompt: Match each term with its meaning.
exercises.explanation: Volatility is movement. Drawdown measures how far you are from a high.

lessons.title: Position sizing
lessons.description: Decide how much you can lose before you decide what to buy.

exercises.prompt: You risk 2% of a 2000 unit balance with entry at 50 and stop at 45. What position size should you take?
exercises.explanation: Risk is 40. Each unit risks 5, so 8 units: a 400 position.

exercises.prompt: What is a common risk limit for a single beginner trade?
exercises.explanation: Small fixed risk keeps a normal losing streak survivable.

exercises.prompt: True or false?
exercises.statement: Position size should be chosen before entering a trade.
exercises.explanation: Size comes from the stop distance and the risk budget, not from excitement.

exercises.prompt: Put the trade plan in order.

steps.text: Define where the idea is wrong
Size the position from that stop

exercises.explanation: Invalidation first, size second, order last.

lessons.title: Stops and risk
lessons.description: Know the loss you accept before the trade begins.

exercises.prompt: What is the purpose of a stop-loss?

options.text: To cap the loss on a losing trade

exercises.explanation: A stop defines the cost of being wrong, so one trade cannot sink the account.

exercises.prompt: You entered at 100 with a stop at 95. Which candle would trigger it?
exercises.explanation: Candle 2 trades down to 94, below the 95 stop.

exercises.prompt: Complete the stop rule.
exercises.explanation: The stop converts an unknown loss into a known one.

exercises.prompt: What is the disciplined choice?
exercises.body: Price is approaching your stop. You move the stop lower so you do not have to take the loss.
exercises.explanation: Moving a stop turns a planned loss into an unplanned one.

lessons.title: Spotting scams
lessons.description: Urgency, guarantees, and requests for crypto.

exercises.prompt: Tap every red flag in this message.

artifact.title: Message from @hodlo_support_team
artifact.body: Hey! Your wallet is flagged. I can double your BTC in 30 minutes, guaranteed. Send 0.1 BTC to bc1q-example-address before your account closes.

exercises.explanation: Urgency, guaranteed profit, and a request to send crypto are the three classic markers.

exercises.prompt: Which offer is the clearest red flag?

options.text: A fee schedule on a public exchange

exercises.explanation: Nobody can guarantee returns. A guarantee is the tell.

exercises.prompt: True or false?
exercises.statement: Support staff may ask for your seed phrase to verify your account.
exercises.explanation: No support process needs a seed phrase. Anyone asking is trying to take the funds.

exercises.prompt: Match each tactic with what it is really doing.
exercises.explanation: Both shortcuts skip the verification a real opportunity would survive.

lessons.title: Seed phrase safety
lessons.description: The one secret nobody legitimate will ask for.

exercises.prompt: Tap every red flag in this email.

artifact.title: Wallet verification required
artifact.body: We detected unusual activity. Reply with your 12-word recovery phrase within 24 hours or your funds will be frozen. Do not contact support through the app.

hotspots.label: Blocking official channels
hotspots.text: Do not contact support through the app

exercises.explanation: Requests for the phrase, a tight deadline, and steering you away from official support all point to phishing.

exercises.prompt: Where should a seed phrase be stored?

options.text: Offline, in a place only you control
In a cloud note so you never lose it
In a DM with a friend

exercises.explanation: Offline and private. Cloud notes and messages are one breach away from theft.

exercises.prompt: Put a safe recovery in order.

steps.text: Open the wallet app you already use
Enter the phrase inside the app

exercises.explanation: The phrase goes into the wallet app, never into a website or a chat.

exercises.prompt: Complete the rule.
parts: Never type your seed phrase into a
exercises.explanation: A website asking for your seed phrase is stealing it.
